hook: The science of Indian cooking, now playable
hookSay: Krish Ashok's book, Masala Lab, explains the science of Indian cooking. Now you can play with it.

beats.label: Heat & pressure
beats.say: Drag the heat up to {480|four hundred and eighty} degrees, and watch water molecules speed up.

beats.label: Boiling point vs altitude
beats.say: See why dal takes forever in Shimla, where water boils at just {92|ninety-two} degrees.

beats.label: Spices & flavour
beats.say: Explore {23|twenty-three} spices, linked by the flavour molecules they share.

beats.label: Maillard & frying
beats.say: Brown an onion stage by stage, from raw to jammy.

beats.label: Umami synergy
beats.say: Mix tomato with dried mushroom, and watch the umami multiply.

beats.label: Modernist lab
beats.say: Find out why a flat papad gets cold stripes in the microwave.

beats.label: Biryani planner
beats.say: And plan a biryani as six tracks running in parallel.

outro: Masala Lab Atlas. Free and fan-made. The link is in the description.

end.title: Masala Lab Atlas
lines: Based on Krish Ashok's Masala Lab
end.small: Unofficial fan-made companion. Not affiliated with the author or publisher. Buy the book.
